text:
alex: Heads-up — spotted a pretty subtle SDK vs REST parity issue while running the sample app for onboarding. The Python client silently drops unknown kwargs and also renamed max_tokens -> max_output_tokens, so our sample app's calls end up using server defaults. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

maya: Ugh. Is that why the sample responses were shorter than expected? :eyes:

alex: Yep. Example from the sample app: `client.generate(model="redwood-13b", prompt=prompt, max_tokens=1024, temperature=0.2)` — in the SDK that param is ignored and the backend sees no max_tokens. REST call with same body works fine.

sam: Also saw different retry behavior — SDK retries on 503 but treats 429 as terminal (no backoff). REST retry policy is 429 -> exponential backoff. We had a user hit rate limits and SDK gave fast failures.

maya: Can you paste the minimal repro?

alex: Sure. From logs on the sample VM: 
```
[2026-03-22T12:01:05Z] sdk: request body: {"model":"redwood-13b","prompt":"...","max_output_tokens":null}
[2026-03-22T12:01:05Z] rest: request body: {"model":"redwood-13b","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}
[2026-03-22T12:01:06Z] sdk: response length 64 tokens (default)
[2026-03-22T12:01:07Z] rest: response length 980 tokens
```

sam: That log proves the param rename mapping is incomplete. We likely added max_output_tokens for the new naming but forgot a compatibility alias.

alex: There's a second related problem: admin-only endpoint `/v1/admin/keys/rotate` is not exposed in the SDK at all. Sample app uses it during provisioning, so when people try the admin flow the SDK throws AttributeError. REST curl works.

maya: Oof. That's a bad onboarding friction — provisioning fails silently. Any stack trace?

alex: `AttributeError: 'RedwoodClient' object has no attribute 'rotate_key'` — sample tries `client.rotate_key(team_id)` during setup.

ci-bot: automated test failure reported: devex/sampleapp:provisioning (flake) — see run 8653. Related to missing admin endpoint.

sam: Proposed fixes: 1) Add compatibility alias for max_tokens -> max_output_tokens in the Python SDK input validation (and in other SDKs), 2) Implement admin.rotate_key() wrapper (or expose admin namespace), 3) Adjust SDK retry policy to mirror REST: treat 429 as retriable with backoff and surface configurable policies. Add unit tests that compare serialized request bodies to a fixture.

maya: Also update quickstart sample code in docs to use the canonical SDK param names OR include a note about backwards compatibility. We should avoid changing sample apps until SDK patch is released.

alex: Agreed. I can open a PR for the alias and a small test this afternoon. sam, can you own the retry policy PR? We should also add an e2e that runs the provisioning flow on CI.

sam: Yep. I'll prototype the retry change and a small test matrix for 429/503/500 behaviors.

maya: I'll update the quickstart snippet to call the REST curl as a fallback and add a short note in onboarding docs about admin endpoints not being in earlier SDK releases.

alex: One more edge case: streaming vs non-streaming behavior — SDK's stream() call buffers the first chunk and only yields after the second chunk for short outputs. REST SSE yields immediately. That may feel like increased latency to users. Include in the test plan.

ci-bot: created issue DEVEX-1189: "python sdk parity: param alias, admin endpoint, retry/backoff, streaming latency" (assigned: alex, sam, maya)

maya: Thanks for the clear repros — please paste the PR links here when ready and tag devex-review. :thumbsup:
